Thanks again for the call today — good alignment on the high-level requirements for an on-prem, air-gapped deployment. Quick recap and proposed next steps:

  - KV cache persistence and safe shutdown/startup procedures for offline ops.
  - SOC2 / audit evidence and host-level attestations required for procurement.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You to share network diagram, rack layout, and any procurement timelines — you mentioned security will need an attestation template.
2) We'll schedule a technical deep-dive with Michael (our infra lead) and Dev (deployment engineer) to review hardware sizing, offline restart procedures, and KMS/HSM integration.
3) I'll follow up with a preliminary hardware spec and an offline-ops runbook draft for review.

Can you confirm whether the racks will have redundant top-of-rack switches and whether remote hands are provided for reboots? Also please attach the network diagram when you have it.

Thanks — talk soon.

Appreciate the attachments — good context. Michael and Dev, thanks for joining. A couple of follow-ups before the deep technical call so we can make the session efficient: 

1) Hardware sizing ask: based on the stated throughput and burst profile, our initial recommendation is:
   - 8 x dual-socket servers with 4 x A100-80GB (or equivalent) per server, NVMe for local checkpointing, 1Gbps management network + 25Gbps data plane between servers.
   - Optional: a modest GPU buffer pool for burst handling (we can size after looking at real traces).

   Michael / Dev — can you confirm if the above is sensible for LegacyBank's expected latency SLOs (p95 < 200ms for 512 tokens)? If not, what would you change?

2) Offline ops & checkpointing:
   - Tom, you mentioned NVMe persistence for KV cache — what are the capacity constraints per host (TBs available)? Also are there constraints around wiping disks for decommissioning?
   - We will draft an offline-ops runbook: safe shutdown ordering, KV flush windows, model cache population steps, and a validation test for service health post-start.

3) KMS/HSM:
   - We support customer-managed KMS in air-gapped modes using on-prem HSM or a sealed key import flow. Do you have a preferred vendor (Thales, AWS CloudHSM in private cloud, etc.)?

4) Meeting cadence: proposed 60-minute deep-dive Tues 2027-06-29 17:00 UTC (10:00 PDT). If that doesn't work, propose alternatives.

Please reply with NVMe sizing and preferred HSM vendor ahead of the call so Michael/Dev can tailor the runbook.

Thanks — quick technical notes prior to the deep-dive.

- Hardware: 8 servers with 4 x A100-80GB each is a reasonable starting point for the throughput target. If p95 latency must stay <200ms for 512 tokens, we should: 
  - Ensure NVLink or similar high-speed interconnect between GPUs in a server for multi-GPU inference shards.
  - Prefer 200Gbps+ RDMA between servers if you plan to shard across hosts; 25Gbps will work for single-host sharding but may increase cross-host latency.

- Checkpointing: NVMe local checkpointing is fine. We recommend:
  - Reserve at least 2–3TB per host for model + KV snapshots depending on model size; please confirm model sizes (we'll send a mapping of model->disk needs).
  - A controlled flush on shutdown (30–90 seconds) to persist active KV state; we can implement a fast-start procedure to replay most recent deltas to keep warm-up under 3 minutes.

- Disk wiping / decommission: We support NIST 800-88 compliant wipes as part of decommissioning runbooks. If LegacyBank requires physically destroying drives, note that will affect replacement timelines.

- KMS/HSM: we have certified integrations for Thales and SafeNet; for air-gapped environments a sealed key import workflow (you generate key in HSM and we consume it locally) is the common approach. Let us know vendor preference.

I'll prepare a short runbook skeleton and a model-to-disk-size table ahead of our Tue call. Looking forward to the deep-dive — the proposed time works for me.

—Michael
